text.p: Grupo Financiero Serfin SA de CV and electrical goods chain store Grupo Elektra SA de CV signed Wednesday an alliance that they said is aimed at promoting savings among low income earners.
Low income earners will soon be able to make deposits through Elektra's 500 stores in Mexico and the money will be handled by Serfin, Mexico's third largest banking group.

Serfin director general Adolfo Lagos said the aim behind the alliance was to give access to the Mexican banking system to "an important strata of society that to date had no real means to save with a formal bank".
Lagos said the alliance would effectively increase Serfin's number of branches to 1,000.
Pedro Padilla, director general of Elektra, said in the following four to five years the alliance hoped to attract between 2.5 and three million new account holders.
